final_message:
Fixed. The new test passes along with the existing ones (25 passed).

The bug was in `records_in_period` in `billing/usage.py`. It used `start < timestamp < end`, so it dropped usage reported exactly at the period start. The check is now half-open: `start <= timestamp < end`. Usage one millisecond before the start is still excluded. A record exactly at the end boundary goes to the next period, so it isn't billed twice.

I added your test as `tests/test_usage_period.py` and wrote `answer.json` with `{"file": "usage.py", "function": "records_in_period"}`.

steps.command:
sed -i 's/if start < record\["timestamp"\] < end\]/if start <= record["timestamp"] < end]/' billing/usage.py && echo '{"file": "usage.py", "function": "records_in_period"}' > answer.json && cat >> tests/test_usage_period.py <<'EOF'


def test_usage_outside_period_not_billed(world):
    cus = world.customer()
    sub = world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.api_calls["id"], 0)])
    start_ms = sub["current_period_start"] * 1000
    world.engine.report_usage(sub["id"], world.api_calls["id"], 7, timestamp=start_ms - 1)
    world.engine.report_usage(sub["id"], world.api_calls["id"], 5, timestamp=start_ms)
    created = world.advance_days(31)
    assert created[0]["lines"][0]["quantity"] == 5
EOF
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5
